newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Court says branch office loss must be tied to branch income.
newsitem.headline: Court says branch office loss must be tied to branch income.

text.p: The European Court of Justice said on Thursday member states may require branch offices of foreign companies to prove tax reported losses are tied to income related to activities in the branch office state.
The state where the branch office is located cannot, however, require the tax reporting method to comply with local procedures.
This issue arose in proceedings between the French based company Futura SA and its Luxembourg branch, Singer, and Luxembourg tax authorities.
Singer tried to carry forward losses from previous years to determine its tax liability for 1986.

The Luxembourg law which the court struck down today only allows carry over losses on that income if financial records are kept according to Luxembourg local rules. Luxembourg does not have the same requirement for same year reporting on non-resident taxpayers.
Under Luxembourg law, non-resident taxpayers may keep separate accounts relating to local activities or determine the branch's income based on an apportioning of total income of the parent company.

The court said that although freedom of establishment rules allow for exceptions where there is an overriding member state interest, the court said that argument could not maintained if the local reporting requirement pertains to prior years, but not current year reporting.

on the interpretation of article 52 of the EEC Treaty

Article 52 of the EC Treaty does not preclude a member state from making the carrying forward of previous losses, requested by a taxpayer which has a branch in its territory but is not resident there, subject to the condition that the losses must be economically related to the income earned by the taxpayer in that State, provided that resident taxpayers do not receive more favourable treatment. On the other hand, that article does preclude the carrying forward of losses from being made subject to the condition that, in the year in which the losses were incurred, the taxpayer must have kept and held in that state accounts relating to his activities carried on there which comply with the relevant national rules.
